newsitem.title: FRANCE: French prosecutor wants sleaze sentences upheld.
newsitem.headline: French prosecutor wants sleaze sentences upheld.

text.p: A French Supreme Court prosecutor demanded on Tuesday that sentences against Lyon's ex-mayor, the mayor of Cannes and a star news broadcaster be upheld in a fraud case symbolising 1980s political corruption.

Justice sources said the Supreme Court's ruling, due on February 6, would set a precedent for probes involving similar fraud cases since the accused argue that the charges date from too long ago to be tried.
If the court rules in their favour, other investigations into political corruption from the 1980s could be shelved under the statute of limitations.

Prosecutor Bruno Cotte urged the court to reject last-ditch appeals after a Lyon court gave former Lyon mayor Michel Noir and Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot suspended 18-month prison terms and hefty fines a year ago for their roles in illicit campaign funding schemes.

Also convicted of being an accomplice to misuse of corporate funds was Patrick Poivre d'Arvor, star broadcaster on the country's main TF1 television channel, who received a 15-month suspended sentence for accepting lavish gifts including Caribbean holidays.

Money and gifts came from corporate funds embezzled by Noir's businessman son-in-law Pierre Botton. Botton, serving a three-and-a-half year jail sentence, has not appealed and was recently reported to have tried to take his life in prison.
Noir, Mouillot and Poivre d'Arvor have appealed to the Supreme Court on technicalities. The court cannot modify the sentences but can either confirm them or order a retrial.

If the sentences are confirmed, Noir, a member of parliament and a former trade minister once tipped as a possible presidential candidate, and Mouillot will be declared ineligible for public office for five years.

In a separate case, Noir is appealing against a 12-month suspended sentence for diverting eight million francs ($1.6 million) of Lyon's municipal funds to finance political campaigns and personal expenses.
Mouillot is in prison, awaiting trial in a separate case on accusations that he extorted money from casinos in his Riviera resort.
